issuer.entity: Financial Reserves and Asset Exploration Inc (Frax Inc)
issuer.scope: Issuer-wide organizational, disclosure and operating judgment; canonical Ethereum is the dashboard's phase-one market and authority scope.
issuer.summary: Frax Inc is the Delaware issuer. Eligible holders can request USD 1 of value, subject to the issuer’s choice of asset, limits and suspension rights. Reserves are intended to benefit holders as a class. Individual reserve title, enforceable priority and funded cash settlement remain unverified. Issuer remains 5.0. The approved FIP-441 issuance and IP license has a distinct scope from FIP-432 operating delegation.
facts: The November 19, 2025 token terms identify Financial Reserves and Asset Exploration Inc (Frax Inc), a Delaware corporation, as issuer. Frax describes it as a public-benefit corporation. FIP-432 (July 7, 2025) assigns compliance, reserve selection, custodian onboarding and fiat redemption operations and calls for annual revenue and expense reporting. Current licensing, directors and delivery of those reports were not independently verified.

FIP-432 provides DAO oversight and a vote to alter delegated operations. FIP-441, posted January 26, 2026 and approved in the Snapshot vote ending February 5, describes an exclusive, perpetual, irrevocable license of frxUSD IP and issuance rights to Frax Inc. These powers have different scopes. The forum also describes quarterly high-level income and cash-flow summaries. A vote establishes policy approval; the executed license, current regulatory authorization and delivery of summaries remain unverified. No later material change to these issuer provisions was identified in the reviewed forum topics through November 27.

The token terms dated November 19, 2025 select Delaware law and exclusive Delaware state or federal courts, subject to arbitration provisions adopted in a separate agreement. FraxNet service terms have a separate perimeter.

Section 7 of the November 19, 2025 terms expresses the issuer’s intent to honor eligible redemptions at USD 1 of value per frxUSD. Frax Inc chooses cash, eligible reserve assets or a combination. It may impose fees, limits, queues or gates and delay or suspend fulfillment in specified circumstances. Secondary market price and immediate par cash settlement are not guaranteed.

Fiat rails require onboarding and KYC/KYB. Taking a specific fund token may require whitelisting or accreditation and depends on custodian inventory. The documented Ethereum USDC route uses USTB internally without requiring the user to receive USTB. Current route capacity and settlement were not measured.

The token terms intend reserves held in RWA custodian structures to benefit holders collectively and fund redemption and wind-down ahead of general unsecured creditors. Mandatory higher-ranking claims, actual structures and court rulings can override that intent. Holding frxUSD grants no direct title or security interest in a particular reserve. Bankruptcy remoteness and recovery amount are unverified.

At the November 27, 2026 03:43:47 UTC issuer-sheet snapshot, Frax published a multichain assets and liabilities disclosure. Erebor cash is issuer-reported. A BitGo balance for WTGXX cannot establish beneficial ownership by itself. No signed comprehensive independent financial audit or reserve opinion was identified in the reviewed materials. Complete global liabilities, remote token supplies and bridge lockbox offsets were not independently reconciled here. Code reviews and public reserve verification have separate scopes.

Dated shared DeFiLlama record at 2026-11-03T09:00:07Z: reserves $98,767,291.03, liabilities 95,494,024.11 frxUSD; producer par coverage 103.43% versus market-liability coverage 103.45%. Independent global coverage remains withheld.

Shared producer concentration: WTGXX 68.56%, BUIDL 16.08%, USTB 12.57%, Erebor cash 2.03%, USDC 0.66%, AUSD 0.10% and USDB dust. The immutable source, exact percentages and clocks are carried in shared_evidence.
Zellic published a July 2025 Frax review covering the original frxUSD and custodian system and a February 2026 review covering newer frxUSD infrastructure and cross-chain components.
The Ethereum owner changed in August 2026 from a 3-of-5 Safe to a 4-of-7 Safe with no signer overlap; the reviewed assessment did not locate the governance record authorizing that handover.
Frax now reports frxUSD supply across more than 30 networks, while the accepted authority evidence covers only a subset; unwalked deployments are unmeasured rather than clean.
Contract powers, delay enforcement and audited-code deployment identity are priced on Contract & Admin rather than counted again on Issuer.

DeFiLlama now claims reserve verification including BitGo WTGXX and Erebor cash; this is not BM reproduced offchain assurance, beneficial-ownership proof, an audit or complete independently reconstructed global liabilities. sfrxUSD receives upstream context only.

November 3 reserve/disclosure facts adopt the same BM immutable shared snapshot; historical issuer/governance judgment and issuer_score_generated_at are unchanged.
issuer.producer_note: Shared evidence adoption only: source classes and clocks preserved; authored Issuer 5.0, full verification and score-decision clock unchanged. No separate scraper, coverage/concentration calculation, live widget or schedule.
